title: Thermal management: chillers · cooling towers · chilled water · MAU · DCC · waste-heat recovery
flow_order: Chiller evaporator ↔ chilled water (CHW) supply/return ↔ MAU cooling and dehumidifying coils / DCC (sensible heat removal) / primary side of PCW heat exchangers | Chiller condenser ↔ condenser water (CW) supply/return ↔ cooling tower (heat rejected to atmosphere) | Air: outdoor air → MAU (preheat, humidify, cool/dehumidify, reheat) → plenum → FFU → cleanroom → below the floor → DCC in the return shaft → plenum | Optional: condenser heat and return-water heat → heat-recovery chiller / heat exchanger → hot water for MAU reheat and winter preheat
typical_values_from_literature: Chilled water for MAU cooling coils about 5–7 °C (paper); in dual-temperature chilled water systems, low temperature about 6–7 °C (MAU) and high temperature about 15–18 °C (DCC) (company technical article) | MAU sequence in the literature: fan → preheat coil → precool coil → humidifier (air washer) → cooling coil → reheat coil | The DCC runs with the coil surface above the return-air dew point so that no condensation forms (hence 'dry')
public_facts_about_pyeongtaek: Satellite imagery shows the fan cell arrays of the four cooling tower banks east of P1 and P2, and water vapour over the utility building between P3 and P4 and the north utility area (grades B and C) | Disclosed and reported: Samsung E&A performed the Pyeongtaek P2 UT building and the P3 green building, UT building, rooftop exhaust and UPW (grade A: existence) | 'P4 Ph4 DCC section 1' appears in a contract name in a filing (grade A: existence of DCC work) | Samsung Electronics Sustainability Report (2023): at Giheung, Hwaseong and Pyeongtaek, waste heat from equipment cooling water and wastewater effluent is recovered and reused as a heat source for process water and HVAC (grade A: existence of waste-heat recovery) | Geothermal heating/cooling at the Pyeongtaek site: 200 RT (2021 and 2022 reports) → 738 RT (2023 report). Installed under some buildings at Hwaseong and Pyeongtaek (press). Location is not public
limits: Chiller type, count and capacity, chilled water temperature set points, whether waste-heat recovery is applied, and actual pipe routes are not public. Placing chillers in the utility building and the fab connection points are assumptions. Chilled water headers are placed in the return-shaft bands and the central core and do not cross above the FFU ceiling (whether this reduces the risk of water leaks falling into the cleanroom is a review hypothesis).

title: PCW: process cooling water closed loop
flow_order: PCW heat exchanger (secondary side) → circulation pump → supply header → bay branches → tools, dry pumps, scrubbers, RF power → return header → heat exchanger | The primary side of the heat exchanger is chilled water (CHW) or cooling tower water. PCW is a closed loop dedicated to tools; it is not consumed or discharged in normal operation
typical_values_from_literature: Required temperature in the literature about 13–20 °C (paper) | Measured benchmark case (a fab in Taiwan): supply 17.8 °C, return 21 °C, flow 1,121.9 ㎥/h, cooling capacity 1,187 RT | Check: Q = ρ·V·cp·ΔT = 1000 × (1121.9/3600) × 4.186 × 3.2 ≈ 4,175 kW ≈ 1,187 RT (3.517 kW/RT) → matches the literature figure
public_facts_about_pyeongtaek: PCW temperature, flow and redundancy for Pyeongtaek P1–P4 could not be confirmed from public sources.
limits: Heat exchanger locations (1F and 5F FSF support zones) and header and branch positions are all concept. This is not the result of a hydraulic analysis with pipe sizing or flow calculation.

title: Gas: bulk gas · specialty gas · filling (transfer) and exchange points
flow_order: Bulk gas: nearby gas-company plant (air separation unit) → underground pipeline → campus entry → (backup liquid storage and vaporization) → purification → fab CSF header → tools | Specialty gas: delivery of cylinders and bulk containers → gas cabinet or BSGS → distribution (VMB) → tool gas box. Purge and cabinet exhaust are separate systems | Distinction of tasks: bulk storage has a 'transfer/filling connection'; cylinders have an 'exchange work area' (cylinders are not filled on site)
typical_values_from_literature: Figures such as pressure, purity and storage quantity vary by supplier and process and are not included in this model (unsupported figures excluded).
public_facts_about_pyeongtaek: Newsis site article, 2022-09: the campus has a large GCS (Gas Chemical System) building storing the gases and chemicals used in production, which are supplied to the production lines through connecting bridges only when needed, for safety (grade A: existence of the GCS building and supply bridges; the article does not say which building) | Gas supply for P1–P4 is split among Air Products, Linde and Air First (press). P1 is Air Products Korea (press); the P3 bulk gas supplier is Air First (press) | The Air First Pyeongtaek plant (about 200,000㎡) is about 1 km in a straight line from the campus and supplies oxygen, nitrogen, argon and hydrogen by underground pipeline (press 2026-05) | Linde announced an eighth air separation unit at Pyeongtaek for additional ultra-high-purity gases and hydrogen (press) | 'P4 Ph4 S-GAS section 1' appears in a contract name in a filing (existence of specialty-gas work) | Plant locations of the three gas companies (Kakao Map): Air Products Korea immediately northeast of the campus, Linde Korea to the southwest, Air First about 1 km to the south → entries from three directions are shown | Linde Korea, Air First and Air Products Korea are also due to move into the Pyeongtaek Advanced Complex General Industrial Park, 460,000㎡ around Bangchuk-ri, Godeok-myeon, south of the campus (press) | Pyeongtaek city supplies treated water from the Godeok public sewage treatment plant to these three gas companies as industrial cooling water: 3.23 km pipeline, 50 cm diameter, 24,400 t a day planned (press 2026-10)
limits: Storage locations inside the campus, entry points, pipe routes and gas-room locations are not public. The yard, gas rooms and mains are concept markers at arbitrary locations.

title: Hazardous emissions (air): exhaust segregation and treatment
flow_order: Process tool → (where needed) dry pump and POU treatment → dedicated exhaust header matching the stream → central treatment equipment → fan → stack (treated exhaust) | Segregation: acid / alkali (ammonia) / organic (VOC, solvent) / heat and general. Mixing causes reactions and solids, so they are collected separately | POU → rooftop scrubber → stack is one of several arrangements; the type and presence of POU depend on the process
typical_values_from_literature: Exhaust classification in the literature: heat/general / acid / (optional) ammonia / VOC. Heat exhaust is often released without treatment (patent literature) | VOC: zeolite concentrator rotor + thermal oxidizer; acid and alkali: central wet scrubber (paper) | Acid gases are treated in wet scrubbers by contact with a neutralizing solution (vendor technical material)
public_facts_about_pyeongtaek: Press that Samsung Engineering handled P3 'rooftop exhaust' (grade A: existence of rooftop exhaust equipment) | Satellite and drone imagery shows steel racks and rows of equipment on the fab rooftop perimeter bands (grades B and C) | Samsung Electronics Sustainability Report (2023): semiconductor sites abate process gases (F-gases) with POU scrubbers and rooftop RCS (regenerative catalytic systems) (grade A: existence of the equipment type; count and location at Pyeongtaek not public)
limits: Which system is on which rack, and the type, count and efficiency of treatment equipment, are not public. South = acid/alkali and north = organic/heat is an assumption for explanation (one review opinion holds that an east/west split may shorten routes, but this is unsupported).

title: Hazardous emissions (water): segregated collection and treatment of wastewater
flow_order: Sources (cleaning, CMP, scrubber drains) → segregated collection by composition (fluoride / acid-alkali / organic …) → transfer by stream → the corresponding treatment stage in the green building | Treated water → public wastewater treatment plant → discharge to stream. Part is reused on site
typical_values_from_literature: Treatment process figures (chemical doses, retention time, etc.) are not included.
public_facts_about_pyeongtaek: Introduction to an official Samsung Semiconductor video (series Ep. 5): the Pyeongtaek campus wastewater plant has a '2.6 km underground passage', screen doors that prevent leaks and a 24-hour control room (grade A: existence of the underground passage; route not public) | The Pyeongtaek campus has two green buildings, an underground water treatment area of about 34,000㎡, purifies about 70,000 t a day on average, and about 97% of the work is automated (press 2021) | As of 2020 the Pyeongtaek campus used about 67,000 t a day on average, and about 54,000 t was discharged to Seojeongni stream via the Pyeongtaek city wastewater treatment plant (press) | Samsung Electronics company-wide water flow in 2024 (thousand t): surface water 187,626 → on-site treatment 59,569 and off-site treatment 92,540; reuse 125,463 (sustainability data)
limits: Which buildings are the green buildings (S1 and S2 are estimates), the stream classification, treatment process and transfer routes are not public. The underground trench is drawn above ground so that it is visible.

title: Chemical supply: unloading · storage · central supply (CCSS)
flow_order: Tanker unloading bay (quality check) → storage tank → central chemical supply system (CCSS) → double-contained piping → supply unit in the fab FSF → distribution (VMB) → clean and track tools | CMP slurry is supplied in a loop that keeps circulating from the supply room to near the tool to prevent settling
typical_values_from_literature: Pressure, flow velocity and purity figures are not included.
public_facts_about_pyeongtaek: Press citing a brokerage report: STI CCSS was supplied to Pyeongtaek fab 3 Ph3 and Ph4 and fab 4 Ph1 and Ph2 | Hanyang ENG disclosed a P5 piping contract (press 2026-09)
limits: The unloading bay, storage location and pipe routes are not public. Placement at the west end of the utility building is arbitrary.

title: Ultrapure water (UPW) and reclaimed water
flow_order: Industrial water → pretreatment → reverse osmosis, ion exchange, degassing → UPW storage → polishing → fab circulation loop (supply/return) → tools | Low-concentration rinse drain is collected separately and reused via a recovery plant (returned to raw water or utility water, not directly to UPW)
typical_values_from_literature: Water quality and recovery-rate figures are not included.
public_facts_about_pyeongtaek: The Pyeongtaek campus (with fabs 1 and 2 operating) receives 220,000 t of industrial water a day and would need a further 250,000 t a day with up to fab 6 operating (press 2020 and 2024). Raw water is from the Han River Paldang system (press 2022: about 300,000 t a day in total for Giheung, Hwaseong and Pyeongtaek is taken at Paldang) | Options for additional water (press 2020): additional supply by K-water (Paldang and Chungju dams; over KRW 1 trillion and over 10 years) or development of Pyeongtaek city's own source (Anseong stream; KRW 334.8 billion, 7 years) | Sewage reuse plan (press 2022): Suwon 280,000 t, Hwaseong Dongtan 2 42,000 t, Osan 50,000 t = 372,000 t a day to the Godeok (Pyeongtaek) site, dedicated pipeline about 60 km, about KRW 600 billion, from 2030 | Press 2026-09: reuse projects of about 120,000 t a day from Hwaseong and Osan and about 210,000 t a day from Suwon are in preparation (about 330,000 t in total) | Industrial water use at the Pyeongtaek campus: about 120,000 t a day as of November 2022 (local press) | Agreement of 2022-11: plan to supply 372,000 t a day of treated sewage from Suwon, Hwaseong and Osan to the Pyeongtaek campus and 102,000 t to Giheung and Hwaseong (474,000 t in total) | Press that Samsung Engineering handled P3 UPW (grade A: existence)
limits: The location, capacity and loop arrangement of the UPW plant are not public. Placement in the utility building is an assumption. The points where industrial and reclaimed water enter the campus and the pipeline routes are also not public and are marked arbitrarily on the north boundary. The press figures (220,000 t and 120,000 t) differ in date and basis (supply vs. use).

title: Power: receiving · transformation · distribution · UPS · emergency power
systems: ELEC.HV; ELEC.MV; ELEC.LV; ELEC.UPS; ELEC.EMERG; ELEC.PV
flow_order: KEPCO transmission grid (345 kV and 154 kV) → receiving and transformation (GIS, main transformers) → medium-voltage distribution (dual feeders) → fab electrical-room transformers → low-voltage switchboards and busduct → loads | Selected critical loads ← UPS and voltage-sag compensation / selected emergency loads ← transfer equipment ← emergency generators | UPS and emergency generators do not carry the whole fab process load
typical_values_from_literature: The campus distribution voltage (22.9 kV) assumes the usual Korean medium-voltage distribution level; the site value was not confirmed.
public_facts_about_pyeongtaek: The KEPCO Godeok substation is across one road from the campus, has 1 basement and 4 floors above ground and a total floor area of about 100,000㎡, supplies 345 kV, with substation 1 operating from 2016 and substation 2 from 2022, on land provided by Samsung (Seoul Economic Daily, 2024-12). OpenStreetMap also records a 'Godeok substation' lot and three buildings south of P4, and the model location was corrected to that boundary (grades A and B) | 345 kV Godeok #2 substation: 302 Jije-dong, Pyeongtaek; site 102,076㎡, total floor area 17,853.72㎡, one substation building (1 basement, 4 floors above ground), cable tunnel and ventilation shafts, completed 2022-11 (track-record material of the contractor Tongyang) | Site article, 2018: the Godeok substation and the HVDC converter station stand side by side, with a 345 kV transformer room and a 154 kV GIS room inside | 345 kV Godeok–Seoanseong: 10.2 km overhead (35 towers) + 13.3 km underground = 23.5 km. 500 kV Bukdangjin–Godeok HVDC, 34.2 km underground (stage 1, 1.5 GW, 2020-12; stage 2, 1.5 GW) | 'Pyeongtaek 345 kV substation new construction' ordered by Samsung Electronics (HL D&I Halla, KRW 142.9 billion, block A4-1 of the general industrial park in the Godeok International Planning District, 2023-12 to 2026-08, contract filing) | Complex 2 (lines 5 and 6): KEPCO–Samsung agreement (2022-09) — two new 345 kV substations, with 154 kV lines to the fabs, KRW 1.1971 trillion | KEPCO residents' briefing (2024-08): Pyeongtaek currently has 2,300 MW of supply and needs a further 3,637 MW by 2034, including 2,000 MW for the Samsung Pyeongtaek campus → 345 kV Sinpyeongtaek and Godeok 3 substations (target 2031-09; Godeok 3 on a KEPCO lot in the Godeok district) | Official video (2026-06) shows blue solar panels on the roof of a low building beside a fab (which building could not be identified) | Parking-lot solar: 0.4 MW at the Pyeongtaek site (2021 and 2022 reports) + 0.2 MW (added 2022) → 0.7 MW (2024 report). Press: power from parking-lot panels is not used for production lines | 345 kV Godeok–Seoanseong transmission line (23.5 km) completed 2023-09-12 → power supply capacity of 2 GW for P1–P4 (power-industry press) | Samsung Electronics bore the construction cost of about KRW 390 billion for this line; until then the transmission lines to the Pyeongtaek campus were 154 kV (press) | Press 2018: fab 2 can be supplied by the 154 kV Godeok–Pyeongtaek and Songtan–Jinwi lines; fabs 3 and 4 require the 345 kV line first | The Godeok substation has a 345 kV transformer room and a 154 kV GIS room (power-industry site article, 2018) | The 500 kV Bukdangjin–Godeok HVDC (34.2 km underground, 3 GW) supplies the Pyeongtaek area (press)
limits: The exact location of receiving equipment, redundancy arrangement, and the capacity and coverage of transformers, UPS and generators are not public. Which of the three substation buildings is substation 1, substation 2 or the HVDC converter station, the voltage the campus receives (154 kV or 345 kV) and the location of receiving equipment inside the campus were not confirmed. Feeder routes are concept. The solar canopy location is an estimate based on a blue-grey roof in satellite imagery. Placing electrical rooms only in the north support zone is a simplification; one opinion holds that distributed placement should be considered in a long fab because of low-voltage drop (review hypothesis).
